title: Variational Quantum Algorithms in the era of Early Fault Tolerance
problem: Emerging 10,000-qubit devices with ~0.1% two-qubit error rates enable lightweight quantum error correction (QEC) but cannot afford the full qubit overhead of surface codes near threshold, leaving a regime—Early Fault Tolerance (EFT)—where error correction is partial and resource allocation strategy is unclear. Variational Quantum Algorithms (VQAs) must be adapted to exploit EFT resources efficiently without the hardware or qubit budget of full fault tolerance.
motivation: Quantum computing roadmaps predict EFT devices within 3–5 years, and VQAs are among the most promising near-term applications, but running them without a principled EFT compilation/error-correction strategy wastes qubits and leaves significant fidelity improvements on the table.
method: The work introduces partial QEC (pQEC) for VQAs in the EFT regime, which error-corrects Clifford operations using lightweight codes while performing non-Clifford (Rz) rotations via magic state injection rather than the more expensive T-state distillation. Architectural optimizations reduce circuit latency by 2x, and a qubit packing strategy achieves 66% qubit efficiency in the EFT regime. The approach is evaluated by comparing fidelity gains of pQEC-VQA against standard (uncorrected) VQA approaches across multiple EFT device parameter settings.
key_novelty: Adapting partial quantum error correction—Clifford-corrected with magic-state-injected non-Clifford rotations—to Variational Quantum Algorithms in the Early Fault Tolerance regime, achieving 9.27x fidelity improvement without requiring full surface-code QEC overhead.
contributions: Definition and characterization of the EFT-VQA problem setting, bridging NISQ and full fault-tolerant quantum computing.
pQEC strategy for VQAs: error-correcting Clifford operations while substituting T-state distillation with magic state injection for Rz rotations, reducing qubit and gate overhead.
Architectural optimizations reducing EFT-VQA circuit latency by 2x.
Demonstration of 9.27x fidelity improvement over standard VQA approaches and 66% qubit packing efficiency in the EFT regime.

metrics.other: 2x circuit latency reduction; 66% qubit packing efficiency

limitations: Results are simulation-based; no physical hardware implementation is demonstrated on actual EFT devices.
primary_theme: Partial quantum error correction for variational algorithms in early fault tolerance
